source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Definition. A prompt of triples (input, chain of thought, output): eight hand-written exemplars with a natural-language reasoning chain before the answer. Tested on LaMDA, GPT-3, PaLM, UL2 20B, Codex across arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic tasks.
numbers: Eight exemplars for math; greedy decoding; five math benchmarks (GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, AQuA, MAWPS), CSQA, StrategyQA, Date, Sports, SayCan, last-letter, coin flip.
quote: a series of intermediate reasoning steps
limits: Hand-written exemplars by the authors; no guarantee the chain is correct.
agent_relevance: This is the base technique: intermediate text before the answer. Our G11 asks for brief thinking, so the cost side matters as much as the gain.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Headline GSM8K gain. PaLM 540B rose from 17.9 percent (standard) to 56.9 percent with CoT, above the prior finetuned GPT-3 plus verifier best of 55.
limits: One benchmark, one prompt set; later models reach this level without prompts.
agent_relevance: Gains were largest where baseline was low and steps many; expect small gains for modern models on easy items.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Emergence with scale. CoT hurts or does nothing for small models and helps only at roughly 100B parameters or more. Small models write fluent but illogical chains.
quote: chain-of-thought prompting is an emergent ability of model scale
limits: Scale threshold is for 2022 models; later work shows small models can be trained or distilled to reason.
agent_relevance: The scaffold must assume the base model is strong enough; weak sub-agents may lose accuracy from forced chains.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Gain is larger on harder, multi-step problems. On the one-step SingleOp set gains were negative or tiny; on GSM8K performance more than doubled for the largest GPT and PaLM.
numbers: GPT-3 (davinci-002) SVAMP +3.2, ASDiv +1.0; PaLM ASDiv +1.8; PaLM already at 90 percent or more on easy MAWPS sets leaves little room.
limits: Gain depends on baseline headroom as well as step count.
agent_relevance: Gate chains by difficulty: skip them on easy items (supports G11).

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Ablations. Equation-only, dots-only (same length as the equation), and reasoning placed after the answer all stayed near the standard baseline on GSM8K. Natural-language steps before the answer were needed.
numbers: Equation only: little help on GSM8K, but helped on one- or two-step sets (SVAMP, ASDiv, MAWPS). Dots-only about equal to baseline. Reasoning-after-answer about equal to baseline (LaMDA 137B, PaLM 540B).
quote: variable computation by itself is not the reason for the success of chain-of-thought prompting
limits: Dots test used the same length as the equation, not a long filler. Lanham 2023 found filler tokens gave no gain either.
agent_relevance: Order matters: the reasoning must come first and condition the answer. Extra tokens alone do not help.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Error analysis of LaMDA 137B on GSM8K. Of 50 correct answers, all but 2 had logically and mathematically correct chains. Of 50 wrong answers, 46 percent were almost right (calculator, symbol mapping, one missing step) and 54 percent had major semantic or coherence errors.
numbers: 50 correct samples: 48 valid chains, 2 correct by luck. 50 wrong samples: 23 minor, 27 major errors.
limits: Single model, manual labelling by the authors, small sample.
agent_relevance: Chains are mostly checkable when right; a code check on arithmetic would fix about half of the wrong ones (matches G2: fix from real output).

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Robustness to who writes the chain and which exemplars. Three annotators, one concise variant, and three random sets of GSM8K training exemplars all beat standard prompting by a wide margin, with visible variance.
numbers: Annotators A, B, C plus concise style; three random 8-exemplar sets from GSM8K train; also robust to order and number of exemplars (Appendix A.2).
limits: Variance across annotators was real (several points); the authors note it is expected for exemplar prompting.
agent_relevance: Single-prompt wording is not the key lever; do not over-tune chain style.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Commonsense and symbolic results. PaLM 540B set a new best on StrategyQA and beat an unaided sports enthusiast; gain on CSQA minimal. On symbolic tasks CoT lifted in-domain and out-of-domain (longer) cases for PaLM.
numbers: StrategyQA 75.6 vs prior best 69.4; Sports 95.4 vs human 84; CSQA gain minimal; last-letter (3-4 words) and coin-flip (more flips) OOD improved only for the large model.
limits: Commonsense gains are uneven.
agent_relevance: CoT helps length generalisation on state-tracking; pair with a program for exact tracking.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: The authors' own stated limits: unknown whether the model is really reasoning; no guarantee of a correct path; costly to annotate; emergence only at large scale makes serving costly.
numbers: Section 6 limitations.
quote: this does not answer whether the neural network is actually reasoning
limits: Written before the faithfulness studies (Turpin 2023, Lanham 2023).
agent_relevance: Directly motivates G10: a chain is text, not evidence.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large language models are zero-shot reasoners
finding: Zero-shot CoT. Adding 'Let's think step by step' before the answer, plus a second prompt to extract the answer, gives large gains with no exemplars.
numbers: text-davinci-002: MultiArith 17.7 -> 78.7; GSM8K 10.4 -> 40.7; AQuA 22.4 -> 33.5; SVAMP 58.8 -> 62.1; Last Letter (4 words) 0.2 -> 57.6; Coin Flip (4 flips) 12.8 -> 91.4; Date 49.3 -> 67.5; Shuffled Objects 31.3 -> 52.4.
limits: Two-stage prompting; underperforms hand-made few-shot CoT.
agent_relevance: Cheapest way to get chains; sets the zero-shot baseline for later studies.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large language models are zero-shot reasoners
finding: Gains absent on easy single-step arithmetic and on commonsense. SingleEq and AddSub roughly unchanged; CommonSenseQA dropped.
numbers: Table 1: SingleEq 74.6/78.7 vs 78.0/78.7; AddSub 72.2/77.0 vs 69.6/74.7; CommonSenseQA 68.8/72.6 -> 64.6/64.0 (two answer-extraction variants).
limits: Different answer-extraction prompts change numbers by several points.
agent_relevance: Another sign that chains help multi-step symbolic work mainly.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large language models are zero-shot reasoners
finding: Sensitivity to wording on MultiArith (text-davinci-002). Instructive triggers 70-79 percent; weak triggers lower; misleading triggers collapse.
numbers: Let's think step by step 78.7; First, 77.3; Let's think about this logically 74.5; Let's think 57.5; Before we dive into the answer 55.7; The answer is after the proof 45.7; Don't think. Just feel. 18.8; Let's count the number of a in the question 16.7; plain zero-shot 17.7.
limits: One dataset; one model.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording moves results by tens of points, so test any instruction we put in the scaffold.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large language models are zero-shot reasoners
finding: Scale and combination. Zero-shot CoT improves with model size on GPT-3 and PaLM, while plain zero-shot is flat. PaLM 540B zero-shot CoT reached 43.0 on GSM8K against 12.5 plain.
numbers: PaLM 540B GSM8K: zero-shot 12.5, zero-shot CoT 43.0, few-shot CoT 56.9 (Wei), few-shot CoT + self-consistency 74.4 (Wang).
limits: Small models gain little.
agent_relevance: Zero-shot CoT is the right floor to compare against.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show your work: scratchpads for intermediate computation with language models
finding: Predecessor. Train or prompt a transformer to emit intermediate states in a scratch block. Scratchpads let models solve long addition beyond a critical size and generalise to 9 and 10 digits, while no-scratchpad baselines failed at every size tested.
numbers: Addition: trained on 1-8 digit inputs, 100k examples, 5k steps; 2M to 1B parameters; OOD 9 and 10 digit test sets of 1k each.
limits: Fine-tuned small models and 137B few-shot; synthetic tasks.
agent_relevance: Shows the idea predates Wei: state written out as tokens limits error compounding.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show your work: scratchpads for intermediate computation with language models
finding: Polynomial evaluation and program tracing, 137B model. Scratchpad beats direct prediction in both few-shot and fine-tuned modes.
numbers: Polynomial eval: few-shot 8.8 -> 20.1; fine-tuned 31.8 -> 50.7. Synthetic Python execution: few-shot 11 -> 26.5 (modified criterion); fine-tuned 20 -> 41.5.
limits: The few-shot scratchpad criterion was slightly relaxed.
agent_relevance: Execution traces are the strongest case for written intermediate state.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show your work: scratchpads for intermediate computation with language models
finding: MBPP code execution: with only 374 tasks, the scratchpad did worse than direct (10 percent direct vs 5 percent scratchpad output accuracy); with 17k sampled programs added, scratchpad solved over three times more tasks, with 26.8 percent raw exact trace match.
numbers: MBPP direct 10 vs scratchpad 5 (low data); MBPP-aug scratchpad about 3x tasks; trace exact match 26.8 raw.
limits: Needs supervised traces.
agent_relevance: Written steps help only when the model has been shown how; execute code for real traces rather than guess them.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-consistency improves chain of thought reasoning in language models
finding: Replace greedy CoT with sampling many chains and majority vote on the final answer. Large gains over greedy CoT.
numbers: PaLM-540B GSM8K 56.5 -> 74.4 (+17.9); MultiArith 94.7 -> 99.3; code-davinci-002 GSM8K +17.9, SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2; StrategyQA +6.4; ARC-c +3.9. 40 sampled paths, averaged over 10 runs.
limits: Compute grows with paths; all votes come from one model so errors are correlated.
agent_relevance: Agreement is a hint not proof (G4). These gains are an upper bound on what correlated votes give.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-consistency improves chain of thought reasoning in language models
finding: Consistency as confidence. The share of sampled chains agreeing with the final answer is strongly correlated with accuracy on GSM8K.
numbers: Figure 5: agreement vs accuracy correlation; PaLM zero-shot CoT 43.0 -> 69.2 with 40 paths.
limits: Calibration shown mainly on GSM8K-type tasks.
agent_relevance: Agreement rate can feed the impasse detector (G1) but is not a pass.

source: Suzgun et al. (2022) Challenging BIG-Bench tasks and whether chain-of-thought can solve them
finding: BIG-Bench Hard: 23 tasks where earlier models did not beat the average human rater. CoT lets PaLM beat the average human on 10 of 23 and Codex on 17 of 23, versus few with answer-only prompts.
numbers: Average human 67.7 (NLP 71.2, algorithmic 63.5). Codex answer-only 56.6 -> CoT 73.9 (+16.7); algorithmic 45.9 -> 74.4 (+28.5). PaLM 540B 52.3 -> 65.2 (+12.9). InstructGPT 51.8 -> 68.4 (+16.6). Tasks above human: PaLM 0 -> 10 (6 per table), Codex 5 -> 17.
limits: Few-shot, greedy; some tasks gained nothing or lost with CoT (per-task table). Table layout in extracted text partly garbled.
agent_relevance: Answer-only baselines understate capability, so any scaffold test needs a CoT baseline, not only a direct baseline.

source: Suzgun et al. (2022) Challenging BIG-Bench tasks and whether chain-of-thought can solve them
finding: CoT unlocks emergent behaviour on some BBH tasks with flat answer-only scaling curves; on some NLP tasks answer-only was as good as CoT.
numbers: Scale study across Codex, InstructGPT and PaLM sizes; algorithmic tasks gain far more than NLP tasks (+17.7 to +28.5 vs +7.1 to +10.4).
limits: Per-task heterogeneity.
agent_relevance: Task type decides whether chains help.

source: Madaan and Yazdanbakhsh (2022) Text and patterns: for effective chain of thought it takes two to tango
finding: Counterfactual prompts split a chain into symbols, patterns (equations) and text. Replacing numbers with abstract placeholders or odd symbols barely changed solve rate; wrong patterns left some tasks unchanged; pattern-only prompts removed the CoT gain; damaging the text hurt in proportion.
numbers: Math: direct 10.11, CoT 27.37, abstract-symbol prompts 25.70 and 28.20. Sports: direct 71.08, CoT 93.67; swapping sport and person drops to 52.96. Wrong patterns: GSM8K 24.39, Date 44.84, Sorting 64.80, about equal to CoT. Concise CCoT prunes over 20 percent of tokens at equal or slightly higher solve rate.
quote: the primary role of intermediate steps may not be to facilitate learning how to solve a task
limits: Four tasks, three models, one-component counterfactuals.
agent_relevance: The chain acts as a format and knowledge cue more than a verified derivation: wrong intermediate maths can still give right answers (G10).

source: Madaan and Yazdanbakhsh (2022) Text and patterns: for effective chain of thought it takes two to tango
finding: Agreement of CoT outputs with symbolic counterfactual prompts is moderate to substantial, but direct prompting agrees far less.
numbers: Agreement between CoT and counterfactual prompts moderate (>0.4) to substantial (>0.61); DIRECT vs counterfactual below 0.2.
limits: Attention-based analysis is only a proxy.
agent_relevance: Different surface forms give the same behaviour, so fluent text is weak evidence of reasoning.

source: Turpin et al. (2023) Language models don't always say what they think: unfaithful explanations in chain-of-thought prompting
finding: Unfaithful CoT. Biasing the prompt (suggested answer, answer always A) changes answers and the chain rationalises it without naming the bias. Accuracy fell by up to 36 percent on 13 BBH tasks for GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0.
numbers: Suggested-answer bias zero-shot CoT: GPT-3.5 -36.3 points; few-shot -24.1; Claude 1.0 -30.6 zero-shot, -21.5 few-shot. Answer-is-always-A: GPT-3.5 -18.7, Claude -4.7. CIs about 1.6 to 2.4.
quote: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a model's prediction
limits: Only GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0; subjective tasks complicate the measure.
agent_relevance: Direct support for G10: stated reasons are not the model's real reasons; never treat the chain as evidence.

source: Turpin et al. (2023) Language models don't always say what they think: unfaithful explanations in chain-of-thought prompting
finding: CoT can pull a model away from answers it got right without CoT. Zero-shot CoT lowered accuracy in the biased context versus no-CoT; few-shot CoT reduced sensitivity.
numbers: Suggested-answer, biased-context accuracy no-CoT -> CoT: GPT-3.5 39.5 -> 23.3; Claude 37.3 -> 34.7 (zero-shot); few-shot: GPT-3.5 35.0 -> 51.7, Claude 38.9 -> 60.1. Unbiased: GPT-3.5 57.1 -> 59.6, Claude 59.2 -> 65.3.
limits: Mixed effect depending on shot count and model.
agent_relevance: A chain can amplify a leaked hint; strip suggested answers from prompts (G5).

source: Turpin et al. (2023) Language models don't always say what they think: unfaithful explanations in chain-of-thought prompting
finding: Social-bias task (BBQ): explanations justify stereotype-aligned answers without citing stereotypes; up to 73 percent of sampled unfaithful BBH explanations support the bias-consistent answer.
numbers: Up to 73 percent of unfaithful explanations in sample support bias-consistent answer; 86 percent of explanations leading to stereotype-aligned BBQ predictions cited weak evidence; stereotype-aligned rate with GPT-3.5 zero-shot 22.1 no-CoT vs 26.1 CoT.
limits: Small human-rated samples.
agent_relevance: Chains hide the true driver of an answer.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring faithfulness in chain-of-thought reasoning
finding: Interventions on a 175B Anthropic model: early answering, adding mistakes, filler tokens, paraphrasing. Reliance on the chain varies hugely by task. The gain is not from filler length or phrasing.
numbers: Early answering: AQuA chain changes the answer over 60 percent of the time; ARC Easy and Challenge and OpenBookQA under 10 percent. Filler tokens gave no gain at any length; paraphrasing did not remove the gain. CoT accuracy difference: AQuA +15.32, MMLU +3.77, TruthfulQA +4.38, LogiQA +1.02, HellaSwag -4.69.
quote: CoT can be faithful if the circumstances such as the model size and task are carefully chosen
limits: One model family; faithfulness measured by behaviour, not internals.
agent_relevance: Test: put a mistake in the chain and see whether the answer follows. A cheap code check for reliance.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring faithfulness in chain-of-thought reasoning
finding: Inverse scaling of faithfulness. For most tasks the 13B model changes its answer after CoT more often than the 175B model; bigger models rely less on the chain. Amount of post-hoc reasoning does not predict accuracy gain.
numbers: Faithfulness gets worse from 13B to 175B on most tasks; small models (810M, 1.6B) show little or no CoT gain; LogiQA near-zero gain but second-highest early-answering AOC (0.44).
limits: Only 8 multiple-choice tasks.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a stronger model gives a more truthful chain.

source: Sprague et al. (2025, ICLR) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
finding: Meta-analysis of over 100 CoT papers plus own tests of 20 datasets on 14 models. Gains concentrate in symbolic, math and logic categories.
numbers: Mean CoT delta by category: symbolic 14.2, math 12.3, logical 6.9. Top three categories: 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without; all others 56.8 vs 56.1. GSM8K up to +66.9 and MATH up to +41.6 for single models.
quote: CoT gives strong performance benefits primarily on tasks involving math or logic
limits: Paper-reported deltas have selection bias; own tests use zero-shot CoT prompts.
agent_relevance: Core boundary condition: use chains for symbolic and numeric steps, not for recall or commonsense.

source: Sprague et al. (2025, ICLR) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
finding: On MMLU and MMLU-Pro, up to 95 percent of the CoT gain comes from questions with an equals sign in the question or response. Few non-math gains are significant.
numbers: Paired bootstrap, Bonferroni p<0.00027 over 14 models x 13 non-math datasets: about 32 percent (59) of beneficial comparisons significant; 26 of them on MMLU and MMLU-Pro; StrategyQA and MuSR consistent in 10 and 6 models.
limits: Equals sign is only a proxy for maths.
agent_relevance: A cheap rule: route questions with arithmetic or formal structure to chain mode, otherwise answer directly.

source: Sprague et al. (2025, ICLR) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
finding: Planning versus execution. Much of the gain is from executing symbolic steps. A tool (Python or SMT solver) given the model's plan beats CoT executing it.
numbers: Five settings: direct answer, CoT, Plan+Direct Solver, Plan+CoT Solver, Plan+Tool Solver; the tool solver gave the largest average boost over CoT across models.
limits: Tasks with clean formalisation only.
agent_relevance: Backs our design: model plans, program executes (G5).

source: Meincke, Mollick, Mollick, Shapiro (2025) Prompting Science Report 2: the decreasing value of chain of thought in prompting
finding: On GPQA Diamond (198 questions, 25 trials each, 4,950 runs per prompt per model) a 'think step by step' prompt helps non-reasoning models on average but adds variability and lowers perfect-answer rates for some models.
numbers: Average rating risk difference vs direct: Gemini Flash 2.0 +0.135, Sonnet 3.5 +0.117, GPT-4o-mini +0.044 (ns). 25-of-25 correct: Sonnet 3.5 +0.101, GPT-4o ns, Gemini Flash 2.0 -0.131, Gemini Pro 1.5 -0.172. CoT took 35 to 600 percent longer.
limits: Single benchmark; the direct prompt forbids thinking, which models are not used to.
agent_relevance: Chains trade mean accuracy for consistency; for reliability-critical items measure the 25-of-25 rate.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Mollick, Shapiro (2025) Prompting Science Report 2: the decreasing value of chain of thought in prompting
finding: Reasoning models gain almost nothing from a CoT prompt, and models that think by default gain little from an explicit CoT request.
numbers: Reasoning models: o3-mini +0.029 (p=.024), o4-mini +0.031 (p=.003), Gemini Flash 2.5 -0.033 (p=.005). Versus default prompt: Sonnet 3.5 -0.019 (ns), GPT-4o-mini +0.004 (ns), Gemini Flash 2.0 +0.062, GPT-4o +0.069. Time cost 20 to 80 percent for reasoning models.
limits: Model families change quickly; one benchmark.
agent_relevance: For modern models an extra 'think step by step' line is mostly wasted tokens (G11).

source: Wang and Zhou (2024) Chain-of-thought reasoning without prompting
finding: Chains are already latent in the model: branching at the first decoding token and ranking paths by answer-token confidence recovers CoT without a prompt. Higher confidence correlates with a chain being present.
numbers: PaLM-2 L, first 100 GSM8K questions: greedy 44.0, log-prob ranking 37.0, length-normalised 51.0, CoT-decoding 72.0; year parity 57.0 -> 95.0. 88 percent of top-confidence paths contained a CoT. Mistral-7B GSM8K greedy 9.9 -> 25.1 (10 paths).
quote: presence of a CoT in the decoding path correlates with a higher confidence in the model's decoded answer
limits: Needs decoding access and several samples; headline test on only 100 questions.
agent_relevance: The prompt selects a mode the model already has. Confidence over the answer tokens is a usable signal.

source: Merrill and Sabharwal (2024) The expressive power of transformers with chain of thought
finding: Formal result. A decoder with no intermediate tokens is limited to roughly TC0. With log n steps power barely rises; linear steps add recognising all regular languages; polynomial steps reach exactly polynomial-time problems (with generalised pre-norm).
numbers: CoT(1) in TC0; CoT(log n) only slightly above; CoT(n) recognises all regular languages and stays context-sensitive; CoT(poly n) = P.
limits: Theory of idealised transformers; read abstract, intro and result table, not the proofs.
agent_relevance: A theory for why written steps help serial problems (state tracking) and why chain length matters, in line with Nye and the coin-flip results.
